concerns.text: Spec US-2 scenario 2 sets a concrete acceptance condition: "the DOPD regime's drop must be ≤ 20% of the Uniform regime's drop." T008 only *reports* the Uniform-vs-DOPD drop ratio (SC-001); no task's verification step evaluates the ≤20% threshold or records pass/fail against it. The spec's primary hypothesis acceptance criterion is silently dropped.

FR-006 requires logging "training accuracy, convergence steps, and action entropy for every training step." T002's log_step fields are seed, regime, step, episode, loss, entropy, expected_advantage_gap, reward — no per-step training accuracy and no per-step convergence indicator. The training_log contract omits them too, so the FR is semantically weakened to loss/entropy/reward only.

SC-004 requires action entropy measured "against a baseline of random action." T006(b) only asserts DOPD entropy > Uniform entropy; the random-action baseline comparison has no implementing task or verification. Acceptance criterion partially dropped.

T007 uses Mann-Whitney `alternative='greater'` (correct per FR-005's H0: mean(DOPD) ≤ mean(Uniform)), but plan.md T033 prescribes `alternative='less'` and the plan Summary says the test runs on the performance-drop metric, not generalization accuracy. Tasks and plan contradict; align the plan to the spec-consistent tasks version (accuracy, 'greater').

Tasks produce data/processed/teacher_q.npy, v_baseline.json, data/seed_manifest.json, results_seed_{seed}_{regime}.json, sensitivity_report.json, and figures/ — none listed in the data model's file-format table or plan structure. Data model is not the single source of truth for artifacts actually built; update it (or drop the unlisted per-seed JSONs in favor of the CSVs).

Constitution requires every file under data/ to be checksummed with checksums recorded in the project state artifact_hashes map. Tasks.md removed all state writes (correctly platform-owned) but no task computes/records checksums for data/ artifacts. Add a task (or explicit note) assigning checksum generation to a project-owned script so the requirement has an owner.
